tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Kansas District Court Conviction under K.S.A. 21-6614

citations: State v. Anderson, 12 Kan. App. 2d 342, 744 P.2d 143 (1987)
controllingAuthority.summary: A person convicted in Kansas of a traffic infraction, cigarette or tobacco infraction, misdemeanour, class D or E felony, nongrid felony, nondrug grid severity level 6 through 10 felony, drug grid severity level 4 felony for crimes committed between July 1, 1993 and June 30, 2012, or drug grid severity level 5 felony for crimes committed on or after July 1, 2012, may petition the convicting court to expunge the conviction and related arrest records once the applicable period has elapsed since satisfying the sentence imposed or being discharged from probation, a community correctional services programme, parole, postrelease supervision, conditional release or a suspended sentence. Longer periods apply under (c) and (d). At the hearing the court shall order expungement if it makes the four findings in (h). The clock runs from sentence satisfaction or discharge from supervision — not from arrest and not from conviction.

exclusions: Rape, K.S.A. 21-5503 or former 21-3502.
Indecent liberties or aggravated indecent liberties with a child, K.S.A. 21-5506 or former 21-3503 or 21-3504.
Criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504(a)(3) or (a)(4) or former 21-3505(a)(2) or (a)(3).
Aggravated criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504 or former 21-3506.
Indecent solicitation or aggravated indecent solicitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5508 or former 21-3510 or 21-3511.
Sexual exploitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5510 or former 21-3516.
Internet trading or aggravated internet trading in child pornography, K.S.A. 21-5514.
Aggravated incest, K.S.A. 21-5604 or former 21-3603.
Endangering or aggravated endangering a child, K.S.A. 21-5601 or former 21-3608 or 21-3608a.
Abuse of a child, K.S.A. 21-5602 or former 21-3609.
Capital murder, K.S.A. 21-5401 or former 21-3439.
Murder in the first degree, K.S.A. 21-5402 or former 21-3401.
Murder in the second degree, K.S.A. 21-5403 or former 21-3402.
Voluntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5404 or former 21-3403.
Involuntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5405 or former 21-3404.
Sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3517, where the victim was under 18 at the time of the crime.
Aggravated sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3518.
A violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, including any diversion for such violation.

Any conviction for any offence in effect at any time prior to July 1, 2011 that is comparable to any offence in K.S.A. 21-6614(e). This reaches convictions under repealed pre-2011 offence definitions.
An attempt to commit any of the above.

Any conviction or any part of the criminal record of a person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act while registration is required, K.S.A. 21-6614(f), except through the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route.

geography.venue: Statewide statute and statewide forms, executed county by county across 31 judicial districts. K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1) directs the petition to the convicting court. The Judicial Council instructions tell the participant to file with the clerk of the court in the county in which they were arrested. For the ordinary case these are the same county; where they differ, the statute governs and the participant confirms with the clerk.

destination.name: Clerk of the convicting district court
destination.detail: All petitions for expungement are docketed in the original criminal action under K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(3). The Judicial Council instructions nonetheless require a Criminal Cover Sheet, whose own text says it initiates a criminal docket sheet. Provide the cover sheet and do not promise the participant a new case number.

components.notes: Criminal Cover Sheet, revised 10/14/2025, the only current-revision form in the set. The form's own text says a new case will not be accepted without a cover sheet attached. Race, ethnicity and Social Security number are left for the participant.

Petition for Expungement of Conviction or Diversion, Rev. KSJC 08/2022, Option A completed for a conviction. Items 3 through 7 are mechanical identity and case facts. Item 8's option and year selection and item 9's assertion that the offence is not a K.S.A. 21-6614(e) offence are legal conclusions the participant owns; LegalEase presents the statutory lanes and records the participant's selection.

Notice of Hearing on Petition for Expungement of Conviction or Diversion, KSJC 12/2016. Everything except the hearing date, time, courthouse, division and room is completed. The Certificate of Service and Mailing is left blank and labelled for the clerk: it reads in the first person but its signature line is the clerk's, and K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(1) puts notice on the court. Filed as an original plus two copies; the clerk sends them to the prosecutor and the arresting law enforcement agency.
Order of Expungement of Conviction or Diversion Cover Sheet, KSJC 12/2016, for transmission to the Kansas Bureau of Investigation so it can identify the right conviction or diversion to expunge.

Order for Expungement of Conviction or Diversion, Rev. KSJC 08/2022, the granting order. Paragraphs 1 through 4, which recite the participant's own identity and case facts, are completed in advance and the form is brought to the hearing. The findings language and the judge's signature block are left for the court. Once signed the clerk sends a certified copy to the KBI, which notifies the FBI, the Secretary of Corrections and any other criminal justice agency holding a record.

Order Denying Expungement of Conviction or Diversion, KSJC 12/2016. Paragraphs 1 through 4 are completed in advance and the form is brought to the hearing so the judge can sign whichever order applies. Paragraph 8, the reason for denial, is left for the court, as is the "Approved by: Assistant County/District Attorney" block. Preparing the denial order in advance is unusual and is required by the Judicial Council instructions.

Participant instructions and hearing-preparation material: the eleven-step Judicial Council sequence, who completes which document and in what order, how to obtain the hearing date, the copy count to confirm with the clerk, the four K.S.A. 21-6614(h) findings in plain language, and a prompt for the participant to assemble their own account and supporting documents.

participantInputs.question: What is your full legal name?
What was your full name at the time of the arrest, conviction or diversion, if different from your name now?
What sex, race and date of birth should the petition state?
In which Kansas county and which court was the case, and what is the case number?
Which law enforcement agency arrested you?
What offence were you convicted of, and under which Kansas statute?
On what date was the offence committed? This is not the same as the conviction date, and it decides which version of the law applies to you.
On what date were you convicted?
How was the offence classified — a traffic, cigarette or tobacco infraction, a misdemeanour, or a felony? If a felony, what class or grid severity level?
Was the conviction for driving under the influence under K.S.A. 8-1567, and if so was it a first violation or a second or subsequent violation?
On what date did you satisfy the sentence imposed?
On what date were you discharged from probation, a community correctional services programme, parole, postrelease supervision, conditional release or a suspended sentence?
Have you been convicted of a felony in the past two years, or is any felony proceeding pending or being instituted against you?
Are you currently required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act?
Having read the list of offences that cannot be expunged, do you assert that your conviction is not one of them and is not comparable to one of them under a pre-July-2011 offence definition?
In your own words: what has changed in your circumstances and behaviour since the case, and why does expungement matter to you now?
What documents do you have that show what you have been doing since the case — employment, education, treatment, service, letters of support?

rules.filing: File with the clerk of the convicting district court, docketed in the original criminal action, with the Criminal Cover Sheet and the required number of copies. Confirm the copy count with the clerk before filing.
rules.fees: Docket fee $176 under K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(2). The supreme court may additionally impose a charge not exceeding $19 per case to fund non-judicial personnel; 2026 Senate Bill 430 carries that authority from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2030. The docket fee is the only fee that may be collected for the case.
rules.feeWaiver: None in this lane. The only fee waiver in K.S.A. 21-6614 is the specialty court waiver at (a)(3). 2026 House Bill 2724, which would have authorised judges to waive the expungement docket fee on a poverty affidavit, died without enactment, so no general poverty-based statutory waiver exists. Some district courts nonetheless accept a poverty affidavit in practice.
rules.notice: The court sets the hearing date and causes notice to be given to the prosecutor and the arresting law enforcement agency, K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(1). No response or objection period is specified; the prosecutor appears at the hearing.
rules.service: The participant files the Notice of Hearing with the original plus two copies and the clerk sends them to the prosecutor and the arresting law enforcement agency. The participant does not serve and does not sign the certificate.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition, affirming under penalty of perjury that the statements are accurate to the best of their knowledge.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The adopted memorandum directs that source Track A be split into conviction and diversion runtime tracks because the triggering events and waiting-period logic differ even where the document suite overlaps. This is the conviction node. Its trigger is satisfying the sentence imposed or discharge from supervision, its venue is the convicting court, and it carries the full 3, 5, 7 and 10 year lane structure including both DUI lanes. The route is a single official_pdf_fill packet, not a staged hybrid: obtaining a hearing date from the clerk is not a separate legal mechanism, and the hearing details and the clerk's certificate are manual-completion items on a form the packet already generates. The Judicial Council set is the statewide instrument and interlocks; a conforming custom petition would be lawful because K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(1) prescribes contents rather than format, but it should not be used here. The four (h) findings are real and three of them are unpleaded by the official form, which is met with a hearing-preparation document that prompts the participant's own facts and never writes them.

limitations.statement: Capture the date the offence was committed, not only the conviction or diversion date. Under State v. Anderson the law in effect when the offence was committed governs eligibility unless current law is more beneficial to the defendant, and the waiting-period lanes turn on offence-date windows.

provenance.sourceStatement: Under *State v. Anderson*, the law in effect when the offense was committed governs eligibility unless current law is more beneficial to the defendant. The Judicial Council chart works this through for DUI. It applies more broadly, and it means the engine must capture the **date the offense was committed**, not only the conviction date.

limitations.statement: A person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act may not expunge any conviction or any part of their criminal record while registration is required, K.S.A. 21-6614(f). That freezes every case in the record, not only the registrable offence. The sole exception is the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route; sex offender and violent offender registrants are barred with no exception.

provenance.sourceStatement: Except as provided in K.S.A. 22-4908, an offender required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act may not expunge **any** conviction or any part of the criminal record while the registration requirement is in effect. Not just the registrable offense. Every other case is frozen too.

limitations.statement: The packet carries a hearing-preparation document putting the four K.S.A. 21-6614(h) findings in plain language and prompting the participant to assemble their own account of the intervening years and their own supporting documents. controllingAuthority.summary: A person who has fulfilled the terms of a diversion agreement may petition the district court to expunge the diversion agreement and related arrest records if three or more years have elapsed since the terms of the diversion agreement were fulfilled. The five-year lanes in (c) and the five-year first-violation DUI lane in (d)(1) reach diversions by their own terms; the 10-year lane in (d)(2) speaks only of satisfying a sentence or discharge from supervision and does not reach a diversion, which is why the Judicial Council chart shows not-applicable in the diversion column for the 7-year and 10-year DUI rows. The triggering event is fulfilment of the diversion terms, and nothing else.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Immediate Expungement After Completing a Specialty Court Programme, K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(3)
tracks.publicName: Expunging a conviction right after you finish a specialty court programme

controllingAuthority.summary: Notwithstanding the three-year rule in K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1), and except as provided in subsections (b), (c), (d), (e) and (f), a person who has completed the requirements of a specialty court programme established under K.S.A. 20-173 may petition the district court to expunge the conviction and related arrest records. There is no waiting period. The court may waive all or part of the docket fee imposed for filing a petition under this subsection. At the hearing the court need only find that no felony proceeding is presently pending or being instituted against the petitioner under (h)(1)(B); the two-year no-felony-conviction lookback in (h)(1)(A) does not apply to this lane. The other three findings continue to apply.

exclusions: Rape, K.S.A. 21-5503 or former 21-3502.
Indecent liberties or aggravated indecent liberties with a child, K.S.A. 21-5506 or former 21-3503 or 21-3504.
Criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504(a)(3) or (a)(4) or former 21-3505(a)(2) or (a)(3).
Aggravated criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504 or former 21-3506.
Indecent solicitation or aggravated indecent solicitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5508 or former 21-3510 or 21-3511.
Sexual exploitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5510 or former 21-3516.
Internet trading or aggravated internet trading in child pornography, K.S.A. 21-5514.
Aggravated incest, K.S.A. 21-5604 or former 21-3603.
Endangering or aggravated endangering a child, K.S.A. 21-5601 or former 21-3608 or 21-3608a.
Abuse of a child, K.S.A. 21-5602 or former 21-3609.
Capital murder, K.S.A. 21-5401 or former 21-3439.
Murder in the first degree, K.S.A. 21-5402 or former 21-3401.
Murder in the second degree, K.S.A. 21-5403 or former 21-3402.
Voluntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5404 or former 21-3403.
Involuntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5405 or former 21-3404.
Sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3517, where the victim was under 18 at the time of the crime.
Aggravated sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3518.
A violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, including any diversion for such violation.

Any conviction for any offence in effect at any time prior to July 1, 2011 that is comparable to any offence in K.S.A. 21-6614(e). This reaches convictions under repealed pre-2011 offence definitions.
An attempt to commit any of the above.

Any conviction or any part of the criminal record of a person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act while registration is required, K.S.A. 21-6614(f), except through the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route.

Any offence that would sit in the five-year lane under K.S.A. 21-6614(c), the five-year or ten-year DUI lanes under (d), or the one-year prostitution lane under (b). The exceptions in (b), (c), (d), (e) and (f) all continue to apply, so the immediate route reaches only offences that would otherwise sit in the three-year lane.

components.notes: Criminal Cover Sheet, revised 10/14/2025, the only current-revision form in the set. The form's own text says a new case will not be accepted without a cover sheet attached. Race, ethnicity and Social Security number are left for the participant.

Petition for Expungement of Conviction or Diversion, Rev. KSJC 08/2022, Option B completed for a specialty court petition. The Judicial Council chart's plus-sign markers record which offences remain reachable on this lane.

Notice of Hearing on Petition for Expungement of Conviction or Diversion, KSJC 12/2016. Everything except the hearing date, time, courthouse, division and room is completed. The Certificate of Service and Mailing is left blank and labelled for the clerk: it reads in the first person but its signature line is the clerk's, and K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(1) puts notice on the court. Filed as an original plus two copies; the clerk sends them to the prosecutor and the arresting law enforcement agency.
Order of Expungement of Conviction or Diversion Cover Sheet, KSJC 12/2016, for transmission to the Kansas Bureau of Investigation so it can identify the right conviction or diversion to expunge.

Order for Expungement of Conviction or Diversion, Rev. KSJC 08/2022, the granting order. Paragraphs 1 through 4, which recite the participant's own identity and case facts, are completed in advance and the form is brought to the hearing. The findings language and the judge's signature block are left for the court. Once signed the clerk sends a certified copy to the KBI, which notifies the FBI, the Secretary of Corrections and any other criminal justice agency holding a record.

Order Denying Expungement of Conviction or Diversion, KSJC 12/2016. Paragraphs 1 through 4 are completed in advance and the form is brought to the hearing so the judge can sign whichever order applies. Paragraph 8, the reason for denial, is left for the court, as is the "Approved by: Assistant County/District Attorney" block. Preparing the denial order in advance is unusual and is required by the Judicial Council instructions.

Participant instructions and hearing-preparation material: the eleven-step Judicial Council sequence, who completes which document and in what order, how to obtain the hearing date, the copy count to confirm with the clerk, the four K.S.A. 21-6614(h) findings in plain language, and a prompt for the participant to assemble their own account and supporting documents.

controllingAuthority.summary: Any person who has been arrested in Kansas may petition the district court to expunge the arrest record. There is no waiting period. On filing, the court sets a hearing date and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency, and the official court file is separated from other court records and disclosed only to a judge, designated court staff, the prosecuting attorney, the arresting agency or others by court order. At the hearing the court shall order the arrest record and subsequent court proceedings expunged on finding that the arrest occurred because of mistaken identity, that a court found there was no probable cause for the arrest, that the petitioner was found not guilty, or that expungement would be in the best interests of justice and charges have been dismissed or no charges have been or are likely to be filed. This is the correct route for an arrest-only record: K.S.A. 21-6614 expunges a conviction or a diversion and related arrest records, so with neither there is nothing for it to attach to.

tracks.publicName: Expunging a city ordinance conviction or diversion

controllingAuthority.summary: A person convicted of a violation of a city ordinance may petition the convicting municipal court to expunge the conviction and related arrest records once three or more years have elapsed since satisfying the sentence imposed or discharge from probation, parole or a suspended sentence; a person who has fulfilled the terms of a diversion agreement based on a city ordinance violation may petition once three or more years have elapsed since those terms were fulfilled. Longer five-year and ten-year periods apply to the offences listed in (d) and to DUI-equivalent ordinance violations under (e), and a one-year period applies under (c) to a prostitution-equivalent ordinance violation where the petitioner can prove coercion. The court sets a hearing and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency, and shall order expungement on three findings: no felony conviction in the past two years with no such proceeding pending or being instituted, that the petitioner's circumstances and behaviour warrant expungement, and that expungement is consistent with the public welfare. There is no firearms finding, because a municipal ordinance conviction is not a felony.

exclusions: A conviction or diversion for a city ordinance violation that would also constitute a violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, K.S.A. 12-4516(f).
A district court conviction or diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 21-6614.
An arrest with no municipal conviction and no municipal diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 12-4516a.
A petitioner convicted of a felony within the past two years, or against whom such a proceeding is pending or being instituted, K.S.A. 12-4516(h)(1).

controllingAuthority.summary: Any person who has been arrested on a violation of a city ordinance may petition the court to expunge the arrest record. When the petition is filed the court sets a hearing date and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency, and the official court file is separated from other court records and disclosed only to a judge, designated court staff, the prosecuting attorney, the arresting agency or others by court order. A municipal court may prescribe a fee as costs, except that no fee may be charged to a person arrested as a result of being a victim of identity theft. At the hearing the court shall order the arrest record and subsequent court proceedings expunged on finding mistaken identity; that a court found no probable cause for the arrest; that the petitioner was found not guilty; that the arrest was for a violation of an ordinance prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134(a) or (b) adopted before July 1, 2014; or that expungement would be in the best interests of justice and charges have been dismissed or no charges have been or are likely to be filed.

tracks.publicName: Getting off the drug offender registry so your record can be expunged

controllingAuthority.summary: K.S.A. 21-6614(f) bars expungement of any conviction or any part of the criminal record of a person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act while registration is required, except as provided in K.S.A. 22-4908. Under that section a drug offender who has registered for at least five years after the date of parole, discharge or release, or five years from the date of conviction if not confined, may file a verified petition for relief from registration in the district court of the county of conviction. The Judicial Council has developed the petition form the statute requires. On relief the court orders removal from the registry and notifies the KBI within 14 days. Subsection (i) permits the offender to combine the petition for relief with a petition for expungement under K.S.A. 21-6614 where the offence requiring registration is otherwise eligible for expungement. Sex offenders and violent offenders are not authorised to seek relief.

exclusions: Sex offenders and violent offenders required to register. K.S.A. 22-4908 authorises relief for drug offenders only, and K.S.A. 21-6614(f) bars expungement for the rest with no exception.

Time in jail or prison, and time when the offender was not in substantial compliance with registration requirements, does not count.
An offender required to register under K.S.A. 22-4906(k) because of an out-of-state conviction who would still be required to register under the law of the state where the conviction occurred.
A further petition within three years of a denial, unless the court orders a shorter period.

rules.filing: File the verified petition for relief from registration in the district court of the county where you were convicted of the offence requiring registration. Where the offence is otherwise eligible for expungement, the K.S.A. 21-6614 expungement petition may be combined with it.
rules.fees: The docket fee for the registration-relief petition is as provided in K.S.A. 60-2001. Where an expungement petition is combined, the K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(2) docket fee of $176 applies to that petition. A risk assessment, if the court orders one, is at the participant's own expense.
rules.feeWaiver: None identified in K.S.A. 22-4908. The K.S.A. 60-2001 poverty affidavit practice applies to the civil docket fee by its own terms; its reach over the combined expungement fee is unresolved.
rules.notice: When the petition is filed the court sets a hearing date and causes notice to be given to the county or district attorney in the county where the petition is filed. The county or district attorney notifies any living victim of the offence requiring registration whose address is known, or the family of a deceased victim if the family's address is known. The victim or the victim's family cannot be compelled to testify or to provide discovery to the offender.
rules.service: The court causes notice to be given to the county or district attorney. The participant does not serve.
rules.participantSignature: The petition is verified. The petitioner signs, affirming under penalty of perjury that the statements are accurate to the best of their knowledge.
rules.notarization: none stated in the statute or on the form

selfHelpStopConditions: The county or district attorney opposes the petition.
The court orders a risk assessment, or sets a contested evidentiary hearing.
A victim or a victim's family participates in the proceeding.
The participant is a sex offender or violent offender registrant, for whom no relief route exists and for whom K.S.A. 21-6614(f) bars expungement outright.
Whether the five years of substantial compliance have run is disputed, or periods of incarceration or non-compliance are in question.
The participant asks LegalEase to build or argue the clear and convincing showing.
Immigration consequences are in play.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Reclassified from process_guidance to a composed packet on re-review. The review held stage 1 to guidance because relief from registration is discretionary and contested, which the controlling packet-only amendment expressly rejects as a reason to withhold a packet. Current law is decisive the other way: K.S.A. 22-4908(d)(2) prescribes the petition's contents item by item, (d)(1) fixes the venue, (d)(3) directs the Judicial Council to develop the petition form, and the Council has published it at revision 06/2022 together with an order cover sheet for the KBI. Nine of the ten numbered items on that form are the participant's own identity, conviction, registration, compliance and treatment-provider facts. Only item 10 is a rehabilitation and public-safety narrative, and that is a participant-authored statement LegalEase prompts for and formats rather than a reason to suppress the form. The route is composed and sequential because relief from registration and expungement are genuinely distinct filings: different statutes, different venue formulations, different notice sets, a different standard of proof and different fees, joined only by the permission in (i) to combine them. The second unit references the existing conviction node rather than duplicating it. Direct self-help delivery may remain scope-restricted with attorney handoff for the clear and convincing showing and any contested hearing; packet identity is recorded separately from that scope decision.
